name: DarkSide-50
notes: No dedicated INSPIRE experiments-collection record exists for DarkSide-50 (only DarkSide-20k has one, recid 1830577): confirmed via an inspirehep.net/api/experiments query for "legacy_name DarkSide-50" on 2026-09-17, which returned zero hits. external.inspire_experiment is therefore null, not a P0 omission.

Sources disagree on the exact end of operations: the official LNGS facility page states the experiment "operated from 2013 to 2020"; the DarkSide collaboration's own site describes only the construction/first-fill history up to April 2015 without stating an end date; a 2023 paper analyzes "the entire dataset" without giving its end date either. 2020 (the LNGS facility page's figure) is used as the best-sourced end year, flagged approximate.

summary.plain: DarkSide-50 was a dark matter detector holding fifty kilograms of liquid argon, deep under a mountain in Italy. It ran from 2013 to 2020, testing techniques later scaled up for its successor, DarkSide-20k.
summary.technical: Dual-phase liquid argon TPC, ~50 kg active mass, in LNGS Hall C. First physics data (atmospheric argon) from late 2013; refilled with low-radioactivity underground argon in April 2015. Operated overall from 2013 to 2020 per LNGS's own page. Its final published analysis (2023) used the entire low-radioactivity-argon dataset to set a 90% CL limit of 6e-43 cm^2 for a 3 GeV/c^2 WIMP.
